survivorAndItsResolution.firstVerdict: SURVIVED - exit 0, 1 passed. The bundle wrote a transcript containing a live wire token and finalized happily.
survivorAndItsResolution.rootCause: Measured directly, not inferred: SECRET_PATTERNS[1] is /"?token"?\s*[:=]\s*"[^"]{16,}"/i and requires an UNESCAPED quote immediately before the colon. The frame is stored nested as a JSON string field, so its quotes arrive escaped (\"token\":\"...\"). Probe run in-session: the raw frame matches the pattern (true); the same frame nested by JSON.stringify does not (false).
survivorAndItsResolution.decision: REPORT, do not widen the scan. SECRET_PATTERNS is shipped, shared by four packs, and its own jest control row deliberately accepts prose that merely mentions the words - widening it is a behavior change to a guard this unit does not own, with its test suite in src/, outside ownedPaths.
survivorAndItsResolution.fixTaken: The row now asserts its own safety property directly: the transcript body must not contain the role's literal identity.wireToken. Re-running M4a against that assertion gives exit 1, 'future-gm transcript still contains its wire token'. The previously-surviving mutant is dead, and the row no longer delegates a safety property to a guard that cannot see it.
survivorAndItsResolution.residualForASuccessor: The evidence bundle's secret scan is blind to credentials nested inside JSON-encoded string fields. Any future pack that writes a wire transcript through bundle.write() inherits that blindness. Worth a successor ruling; not fixed here.

nonClaims: The transcript is REDACTED, not raw. The campaign join frame carries the role's wire token; the value is replaced before the write, the redaction is recorded inside the artifact, and two assertions prove it ran. The scan was never weakened to make the letter fit.

The projection is POST-WIRE: the viewer-scoped snapshot as DELIVERED to each role, not the projector object before serialization. A pre-serialization capture needs a seam in src/lib/multiplayer/server/projection/, outside ownedPaths. The artifact carries this non-claim in its own body.
The latency artifact is recorded and never gated. E2E-71..74 own the latency budgets and score them on the controlled runner class; a second gate here would be a second, unreviewed one.

attach() has no jest row. jest.config roots are ['<rootDir>/src','<rootDir>/scripts','<rootDir>/openspec'] and e2e/ is not among them; the fixture's suite lives at src/__tests__/unit/evidence/gmTwoPlayerEvidence.test.ts, outside ownedPaths and deliberately not edited. Its proof is the live 27-cell row plus that suite staying 12/12 unchanged.

The trace archive is DEFLATE-compressed, so the latin1 secret scan cannot inspect its entries. Mitigations taken: tracing starts with screenshots, snapshots and sources all false, and every credential in the sandbox is a per-run fixture token the fixture deletes on cleanup. The limit is declared in the attach() doc rather than implied.
